pages.text: The Rune Programmer organizes 29 editable spells as $(thing)theorems$(): ready programs with inspectable formulas and typed graphs.$(br2)The scrollable catalog covers Movement, Sensing, Control, Alchemy, and Metamagic. Hover a theorem for its formula and behavior.$(br2)$(thing)Factored Leap$() is available through the Rune Programmer.

pages.title: Formula Shorthand
pages.text: A formula is a compact summary, not executable or persisted Function source. Its outer verb states the conclusion: $(thing)push$(), $(thing)blink$(), or $(thing)mark$(). Names such as $(thing)self$(), $(thing)look$(), and $(thing)up$() provide values; relations provide evidence.$(br2)Select a theorem to keep its formula above the numbered typed proof.$(br2)For Factored Leap, authored source, checked form, and compiled graph remain distinct. The source defines pure $(thing)halve$(), applies it to observed look and authored up, then lowers to the existing graph. The function does not survive at runtime.

pages.title: Keys And Narrator
pages.text: Tab outlines the palette. Up/Down moves the ivory row; Enter or Space selects. Home/End jumps to an edge.$(br2)The narrator reads name, position, formula or output type, and activation keys.$(br2)The functional Inspector separates authored source, checked form, compiled graph, and diagnostics. Focused rows stay readable in both languages and the compact viewport.

pages.title: Factored Leap
pages.text: $(li)Hop: a short vertical vector.$(li)Dash: look multiplied by 0.8.$(li)Vector Leap: normalized direction plus an upward component.$(li)Recoil: look multiplied by -0.65.$(li)Blink: safe teleport to a ray hit.$(br2)Factored Leap defines pure $(thing)halve$() once, applies it to look and authored up, adds the vectors, then ends at $(thing)push_self$(). Observations stay outside the lambda; beta reduction and lowering remove functional structure before execution.$(br2)Errors or stale authority never partially inscribe an item.

pages.title: Local Movement
pages.text: $(li)Right Angle: a step on the local right axis.$(li)Planar Dash: horizontal forward motion independent of pitch.$(li)Oblique Leap: combines local left, up, and forward.$(br2)These are matrix-style transformations through the player's coordinate frame, not unique movement effects.

pages.title: Higher-order Movement
pages.text: $(li)Harmonic Step: sine and cosine form polar components.$(li)Orthogonal Step: up cross look gives a perpendicular direction.$(li)Quarter Turn: C4 acts on the look vector.$(li)Quadrature Leap: Simpson's rule estimates lift from sampled sine.$(br2)Each conclusion still reaches the ordinary push effect.

pages.title: Sensing
pages.text: $(li)Ray Marker: marks the observed point.$(li)Ore Centroid: marks the mean of #c:ores blocks within radius 5.$(li)Life Centroid: marks the mean of nearby creatures.$(br2)Centroid spells fail without committing the plan when the queried set is empty.

pages.title: Control
pages.text: $(li)Lift: raises the four nearest valid targets.$(li)Hostile Lift: only affects hostile creatures.$(li)Vector Wave: pushes six targets along the look direction.$(li)Horizon Ward: prioritizes the four farthest hostiles.$(br2)Control spells materialize an EffectPlan and normally require amethyst plus force attributes.
